headline: The RBA held rates but warned unions are pushing inflation expectations too high — while last night's NASDAQ surged 1.5% on AI excitement and Anthropic dropped a cheaper, faster Claude model.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL took the biggest hit today, sliding 3.4% as oil analysts cut their price forecasts. The Strait of Hormuz reopening has eased fears about Middle East supply disruptions, and a projected 4.8 million barrel-per-day surplus in 2027 is pushing Brent crude price targets down to the $70–$75 range. Less fear about supply = lower oil prices = energy stocks fall.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dropped nearly 2% today, dragged down by a soft ASX session (the ASX 200 fell 0.64%). As a broadly diversified fund with heavy exposure to both Aussie and international shares, it tends to move with the broader market. The ASX softness today outweighed any overnight US gains that were already priced in.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced nearly 1.8% today — a welcome green day after a tough run. China is reportedly changing its royalty structure for lithium, which has renewed interest in lithium recovery stocks. Analysts are putting lithium back in focus as a quality play, and PLS is the go-to name on the ASX for that exposure.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft gained 1.2% last night in a strong NASDAQ session. The AI story is working hard for MSFT right now — analysts are pointing to its OpenAI partnership as a key advantage, and there's growing coverage of its cybersecurity business as a potential new revenue pillar. The market is rewarding it for having multiple AI-driven growth levers.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two climbed 1.15% last night, riding a solid NASDAQ wave. There's plenty of GTA 6 news swirling — including reports Nintendo is working with Rockstar to bring GTA VI to Switch 2, which would massively expand its addressable market. The noise around GTA 6 keeps investor interest elevated, even as the $80 price point is causing some shareholder debate.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG nudged up 0.58% last night as the broader NASDAQ rallied. Erste Group Bank raised its earnings estimates for Alphabet, a quiet but positive signal. The ongoing debate is whether Google's in-house AI approach (Gemini) gives it an edge over Microsoft's OpenAI bet — sentiment remains cautiously positive.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS was essentially flat today (+0.02%), which is expected — it tracks the US share market but trades on the ASX, so today's price already reflected last night's US session move. The underlying US market (S&P 500) had a strong night, so VTS should benefit when that flows through.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI barely moved today, slipping just 0.17%. Despite all the AI buzz around Anthropic's new Claude Sonnet 5 model, the ETF didn't catch a meaningful bid on the ASX today. The US-listed AI names it holds did better last night, so this may simply be a timing lag.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped a modest 0.22% today. Emerging markets were relatively quiet — the Aussie dollar ticked slightly higher (good for importers, slightly less so for unhedged overseas returns), and there's no major catalyst either way right now.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Energy outlook darkening
watch_today.detail: FUEL dropped 3.4% today and the news backdrop isn't helping. Oil analysts are cutting forecasts with a 4.8 million barrel-per-day surplus projected for 2027 and Brent targets in the $70–$75 range. If you're holding FUEL as a short-term trade, it's worth reassessing. Long-term energy bulls might see this as a dip, but the fundamental headwind is real.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium getting a second look
watch_today.detail: Pilbara bounced 1.79% today on China royalty changes renewing interest in lithium stocks. PLS is still down 24% on your total investment, so it's not out of the woods — but this could be early signs of a floor forming. Worth watching closely this week for follow-through.

watch_today.title: MSFT — AI momentum building
watch_today.detail: Microsoft gained 1.2% last night and the investment case keeps strengthening. Analysts are flagging its OpenAI partnership and expanding cybersecurity revenue as twin growth engines. Your MSFT position is still down 15.8% overall, but the direction of travel looks better. No need to act — but the trend is your friend here.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 on Nintendo Switch 2?
watch_today.detail: Reports emerged last night that Nintendo and Rockstar are working on a GTA VI port for the Switch 2. If true, that's a huge expansion of the addressable audience for Take-Two's biggest release ever. Your TTWO is up 9% overall and had another solid night. This is a hold with upside optionality if the Switch 2 rumour proves true.

watch_today.title: RBA held rates — but watch the language
watch_today.detail: The RBA kept interest rates on hold yesterday but issued a pointed warning that union wage expectations are running too high and could force another rate hike. That's a hawkish signal (meaning they're not ruling out increases) which could weigh on growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on any wage data or union announcements this week.

watch_today.title: Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5 — good news for GXAI.AX
watch_today.detail: Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5 last night, pitched as a cheaper, faster model designed specifically to power AI 'agents' (software that takes actions autonomously, not just chats). The US government also lifted export restrictions on Anthropic's more powerful Fable and Mythos models. More capable, cheaper AI infrastructure is a tailwind for the whole sector your GXAI.AX is invested in.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough Tuesday, falling 0.64% to close at 8,722. Meanwhile last night in the US it was a cracker — the NASDAQ jumped 1.52% to 26,213 and the S&P 500 gained 0.79% to 7,499. The AI rally is the main driver, with tech names broadly higher. Gold pulled back nearly 1% to $3,983/oz as risk appetite improved (investors tend to sell gold when they're feeling confident). Oil is essentially flat at $69.47 a barrel. The Aussie dollar edged up slightly to 68.96 US cents.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech led the charge, up 1.52% last night

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Essentially flat, supply surplus weighing on outlook

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Pulled back as risk appetite improved

politics.summary: The big local story is the RBA — it held rates but fired a warning shot at unions over wage demands. There's also controversy over the Albanese government rejecting most of the UN's human rights recommendations, and business groups are sounding the alarm over rushed industrial relations legislation.

stories.title: RBA holds rates but warns another hike is possible — and points the finger at unions
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA left interest rates on hold yesterday — good news for mortgage holders in the short term — but the tone of the statement was cautious. The Bank specifically called out union wage expectations as running too high, warning they could reignite inflation and force another rate hike. CommBank analysts describe it as the RBA 'playing a waiting game', watching whether wages and inflation behave. For everyday Aussies: your mortgage repayments aren't going up right now, but another hike is still on the table if wages push inflation back up.

stories.title: Albanese government rejects most UN human rights recommendations
stories.source: Human Rights Law Centre / National Indigenous Times
stories.why_it_matters: Australia recently went through a UN Universal Periodic Review — a process where the UN examines a country's human rights record and makes recommendations. The Albanese government has rejected the majority of those recommendations, with Indigenous rights being a key area of concern flagged by the National Indigenous Times. The Human Rights Law Centre is publicly critical of the rejection. This is unlikely to move markets but is a significant political development for those following Indigenous policy and Australia's international standing.

stories.title: Business groups warn rushed IR bill brings 'Victorian disease' to Canberra
stories.why_it_matters: Business lobby groups are sounding the alarm about a new industrial relations (IR) bill being rushed through federal parliament. They're comparing it to Victoria's industrial framework — which they argue gives unions significantly more power over wages and conditions — and warning it could push up costs for employers nationally. If passed, this could affect small business hiring decisions and add to wage pressures that the RBA is already watching closely. Worth keeping an eye on as it moves through Canberra.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Anthropic launching Claude Sonnet 5 — a cheaper, faster model built for AI agents. The US government also lifted export restrictions on Anthropic's most powerful models. Separately, there's growing debate about how governments worldwide should regulate AI.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5 — cheaper AI built to run agents
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic dropped Claude Sonnet 5 last night, positioning it as a more affordable option specifically designed to power AI 'agents' — that's software that doesn't just answer questions but actually takes actions on your behalf (think: booking a meeting, writing and sending an email, running a multi-step research task). The key pitch is it's cheaper to run than previous top-tier models, making it practical for businesses to deploy at scale. Anthropic also has a separate 'Claude Science' product targeting researchers, built around scientific workflows rather than a brand new model. Good news for the AI sector broadly.

stories.title: US lifts export restrictions on Anthropic's most powerful AI models
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has removed export restrictions on Anthropic's two most powerful AI models — called Fable and Mythos. These had previously been restricted from being sold or used internationally due to national security concerns about advanced AI capabilities. Lifting the restrictions means Anthropic can now compete globally with these top-tier models, which is a significant commercial win and signals a shift in US AI export policy toward openness rather than containment.

stories.title: Kids are using AI for homework — and life advice
stories.why_it_matters: A new report highlights that children worldwide are turning to AI chatbots not just for homework help, but for personal advice — including emotional support and guidance on relationships. The trend raises genuine questions about AI's role in child development, the accuracy of advice being given to young users, and what responsibility platforms have. For parents, it's a real conversation worth having with your kids about what AI is good for and where human judgment still matters.

sport.summary: NRL Round 18 kicks off Friday night with Panthers vs Rabbitohs. Wimbledon is underway and Alex de Minaur is through to the second round. The NRL is reportedly closing in on a monster $5.3 billion TV rights deal. Plus, Israel Folau's potential NRL return is generating headlines.

stories.title: NRL reportedly closing in on $5.3 billion TV rights deal
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL is reportedly finalising a $5.3 billion television rights deal, which would be a record-breaking agreement for the game. If confirmed, this would dwarf the current deal and set the league up financially for years to come. More money flowing into the NRL means bigger player salaries, better facilities, and potentially more expansion. Big news for the game's future.

stories.title: Israel Folau could make 'stunning' NRL return
stories.why_it_matters: Rumours are swirling that Israel Folau — who was sensationally sacked by Rugby Australia in 2019 over social media posts and last played NRL in 2014 — could be in talks for a return to the league. The SEN report describes it as a 'stunning' potential comeback. At 37, any return would be remarkable, and it would generate massive media attention whichever club signed him.

stories.title: De Minaur through to Wimbledon second round as one of only two Aussie men
stories.why_it_matters: Alex de Minaur made it through to the Wimbledon second round, joining just one other Australian man to survive day one. It's a solid start for Australia's top men's player, who has been working through some form struggles. Day one of Wimbledon also featured Naomi Osaka and Australian wildcard Maya Joint — who faced Serena Williams in a high-profile first-round match.

stories.title: NRL Round 18 team lists confirmed — Tigers and Eels with notable changes
stories.why_it_matters: Round 18 team lists are out ahead of Friday night's Panthers vs Rabbitohs opener. Fox Sports notes a 'silver lining' for the Tigers despite a shock injury blow, and the Eels have made a significant halves reshuffle that could change how they play this week. If you've got bets or tips locked in, worth checking the full team lists — things can change by kick-off Friday night.
